title: Why Apple just killed the iPhone

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The iPhone is dead because Apple killed it with its own obsession—closed ecosystems and outdated protocols. (3 sec)

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Wrong. Apple’s commitment to security and privacy, like Face ID and end-to-end encryption, keeps the iPhone alive and trusted. (5 sec)

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: But look at the rise of open-source alternatives. Android’s fragmentation and lack of control don’t kill innovation—they fuel it. (5 sec)

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Apple’s hardware-software integration, from M1 chips to seamless app performance, is unmatched and keeps users loyal. (5 sec)

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The iPhone isn’t dying—it’s evolving, and Apple is leading the charge. (4 sec)
